newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 14.

text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Wednesday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Criminal complaint filed against Nomura Securities Co Ltd and three former executives.
-- Three major computer makers to boost shipments of large computers by 30 to 50 percent in fiscal 1997/98.
-- Panel to recommend easing curbs on over-the-counter sale of insurance policies.
-- Prosecutors to question three executives in Nomura Securities Co Ltd payoff scandal.
-- Fiscal reform panel to propose seven percent cut in public works spending in fiscal 1998/99 budget.
-- Major quake hits Kyushu, measuring lower six on Japan scale in Sendai, Kagoshima Prefecture.
-- Education Ministry panel to propose local quotas for national universities.
-- Farm programme to be dropped from supplementary budget.
-- Okinawa to mark 25th anniversary of reversion to Japan. -- Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) reform panel recommends cutting Forestry Agency staffers by more than half.
-- Fair Trade Commission (FTC) warns five elderly nursing homes against unfair ads.
